Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopNova Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing up for questions will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopNova's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jamie Chen, CEO; Taylor Brooks, CFO; and Morgan Lee, COO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jamie Chen, CEO of ShopNova.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by exceptional GMV growth that beat our guidance handily, alongside highly effective marketing campaigns that boosted brand awareness and customer acquisition. Our focus remains on mastering seasonality trends to deliver consistent results across quarters. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our NovaPredict AI platform, which we believe will significantly enhance personalization and drive AOV higher.

Finally, we are committed to optimizing advertising and marketing spend efficiency, with improving ROAS underscoring our disciplined approach.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Brooks, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Jamie. Our Q2 revenue was $1.1 billion, an increase of 22% year-over-year. Gross margin was 28.5%, driven by better product mix in high-margin categories like beauty and apparel, supply chain efficiencies, and take-rate expansion from our marketplace fees. Operating expenses were $850 million, representing 77% of revenue, as we continued to invest in technology and marketing while leveraging scale.

Our net income for the quarter was $120 million, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $2.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance to revenue of $5.0 to $5.2 billion and GMV of $18 to $19 billion.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q2 2024 earnings call. I'll dive right into our core topline metric: Gross Merchandise Value, or GMV, which came in at $4.2 billion for the quarter, marking a strong beat against our guidance.

As a quick recap, during our Q1 call, we guided for Q2 GMV growth of 14% to 17% year-over-year, reflecting a conservative outlook amid persistent macroeconomic headwinds like elevated interest rates in North America and softening consumer sentiment in Europe. On a quarter-over-quarter basis, we expected 5% to 7% growth, accounting for typical seasonality in our direct-to-consumer categories.

I'm pleased to report that we significantly exceeded these targets. Q2 GMV grew 22% year-over-year, well ahead of our 14-17% guidance range, and accelerated 12% quarter-over-quarter from Q1's $3.75 billion—smashing our 5-7% QoQ guide. This represents our strongest quarterly performance since Q4 2021, driven by a combination of tactical execution, technical tailwinds, and resilient demand in high-margin categories.

Let me break this down with some key drivers and regional color. First, category performance fueled the upside. Fashion and apparel, which make up 35% of our GMV, surged 28% YoY, propelled by our AI-powered StyleMatch recommendation engine—similar to Stitch Fix's hybrid model but scaled across our 500+ brand partners like Nike and Levi's. We saw AOV climb 11% to $85, thanks to personalized bundling that increased cart conversion by 18%. Electronics and home goods, at 25% of mix, grew 19% YoY but decelerated QoQ to 9% due to normalizing post-pandemic replenishment cycles, echoing trends at peers like Wayfair. Emerging categories like beauty and quick commerce—now 15% of GMV—exploded 45% YoY, with our 15-minute urban delivery partnerships in 12 major metros mirroring Instacart's playbook and capturing share from DoorDash in non-grocery verticals.

Regionally, the story was one of divergence with upside surprises. North America, our largest market at 55% of GMV, delivered 25% YoY growth to $2.3 billion, beating our internal models by 400bps on the back of back-to-school ramp-up and Father's Day promotions. Active buyers here hit 18 million, up 16% YoY, with repeat purchase rates at a record 62%—a testament to our loyalty program enhancements via Braze-powered omnichannel campaigns. Europe, 25% of GMV, grew a more modest 15% YoY to $1.05 billion, in line with guidance but pressured by 3% inflation drag in the UK and Germany; however, QoQ acceleration to 10% was driven by our localized marketplace launches in Spain and Italy, where we gained 200bps market share per SimilarWeb data. APAC, now 18% of GMV after our aggressive expansion, was the star at 35% YoY growth to $756 million—fueled by live-streaming commerce in Southeast Asia, akin to Pinduoduo's gamified model, where we piloted KOL partnerships yielding 3x uplift in session GMV. Emerging markets like India contributed 8% QoQ growth via UPI payment integrations, offsetting slower traction in China amid regulatory scrutiny.

Technically, our investments are paying off handsomely. We migrated 70% of our storefront to a Kubernetes-orchestrated AWS environment, reducing latency by 40% and enabling 2.5x mobile traffic scaling during peak events like our NovaPrime Days—which generated $450 million in GMV over 48 hours, rivaling Amazon's event metrics on a per-user basis. Machine learning models for dynamic pricing and fraud detection improved gross margin take rates by 150bps to 22.5%, while our supply chain digitization with Manhattan Associates cut fulfillment costs 12% YoY, allowing us to maintain free shipping thresholds competitively.

Strategically, this outperformance validates our Hyperlocal Scale thesis: doubling down on micro-fulfillment centers (now 45 operational) and first-party logistics to combat Amazon's dominance in Prime-like speed. We're also leaning into sustainability, with 25% of Q2 GMV from GreenNova certified products, resonating with Gen Z buyers and boosting NPS by 8 points.

Looking ahead, for Q3, we're raising our full-year GMV growth guidance to 20-23% YoY, implying Q3 at ~$4.5-4.6 billion. This embeds 10-12% QoQ growth, factoring in holiday pre-ramp but mindful of potential US consumer pullback if Fed rates stay elevated.

Thank you, Jamie. I'll now dive into our seasonality dynamics, a hallmark of the E-Commerce landscape that we've navigated effectively to deliver resilient performance. As many of you know, online retail exhibits pronounced seasonality driven by consumer spending cycles—peaking during Black Friday/Cyber Monday (BFCM), the December holiday rush, back-to-school in Q3, and emerging events like Amazon Prime Day or Alibaba's Singles Day. For ShopNova, our full-year Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) of $4.2 billion in FY2023 reflected this, with Q4 alone accounting for 42% of annual GMV, up from 38% in FY2022, underscoring our market share gains in high-velocity categories like consumer electronics, apparel, and beauty.

Let me break down the key trends over the past three years, using our core KPIs: GMV growth, Average Order Value (AOV), order volume, and Active Customer penetration. Peak Season Surge (Q4): GMV grew 28% YoY in Q4 FY2023 to $1.76 billion, fueled by a 22% uplift in order volume to 18.5 million units and a 5% AOV increase to $95, driven by upsell tactics like personalized bundling via our AI recommendation engine. This outperformed the broader industry—think Wayfair's 15% holiday GMV growth or Shopify merchants' aggregate 20% BFCM lift—thanks to our 35% share of traffic from mobile-optimized Lightning Deals, which converted at 4.2%, 60bps above our FY average.

Off-Peak Stability (Q1–Q2): These quarters typically represent 18–22% of annual GMV each. We saw a consistent 12–15% YoY growth here, with Q2 FY2023 hitting $920 million (21% of full-year), bolstered by summer promotions mimicking Shein's fast-fashion drops, yielding 14% order growth despite softer discretionary spend. Emerging Q3 Momentum: Back-to-school and pre-holiday prep pushed Q3 to 25% of GMV in FY2023 ($1.05 billion), with electronics AOV spiking 8% to $120 on laptop and tablet demand, aligning with Best Buy's omnichannel trends.

Regionally, our U.S. segment (75% of GMV) mirrors Amazon's dominance, with BFCM 2023 delivering 32% YoY growth amid 2.5x traffic surges. In APAC (15% of GMV), Singles Day contributed $250 million in incremental GMV, a 40% YoY jump, leveraging partnerships with platforms like Shopee. EMEA (10%) showed resilience with 18% growth, though tempered by VAT hikes and energy costs.

While our trends align with industry benchmarks from eMarketer and Statista—projecting 12–15% global E-Commerce CAGR through 2027—we've seen targeted deviations, which we've proactively addressed. Q1 FY2024 Underperformance (Deviation: -3% YoY GMV Growth): Post-holiday normalization hit harder than the typical 5–7% sequential drop, with GMV at $780 million versus our $810 million guide. Key drivers: Elevated inflation (U.S. CPI at 3.2%) curbed discretionary categories, dropping apparel conversion 150bps to 2.8%. Regionally, EMEA lagged 8% due to sluggish Eurozone recovery. Mitigation: Our inventory optimization via SAP-integrated demand forecasting reduced excess stock by 22% YoY, preserving 400bps of gross margin versus peers like Etsy, who faced 500bps compression.

Q2 Acceleration (Positive Deviation: +18% YoY, 300bps Beat): GMV reached $1.02 billion, exceeding expectations amid Prime Day tailwinds. Deviation explained by our technical initiatives: Launch of NovaPredict AI, a machine learning model processing 1.5 petabytes of first-party data daily, which boosted personalization lift by 25%, driving AOV to $98 (up 6% YoY). This countered macro headwinds like U.S. retail slowdowns (NRF data shows 2% comp-store declines offline), with CAC stable at $28 despite 15% ad cost inflation on Meta and Google.

Q3 Softness Offset (Deviation: Flat YoY, vs. -5% Industry): Back-to-school GMV was $1.03 billion, flat amid supply chain snarls from Red Sea disruptions (adding 10–15% ocean freight costs, per Drewry index). We deviated positively via strategic air freight pivots (up 12% of logistics mix) and vendor-direct fulfillment, akin to Walmart's model, maintaining 98.5% on-time delivery. APAC shone with 25% growth on K-pop merch collabs, while U.S. electronics dipped 2% on softening iPhone demand post-launch cycle.

Seasonality isn't just a challenge—it's our leverage point. We've de-risked deviations through tech stack enhancements: $150 million invested in AWS-based edge computing for real-time dynamic pricing, which captured 8% incremental margin during peaks by adjusting 2 million SKUs hourly. Omnichannel synergies: 25% of Q4 orders originated from our 500 physical micro-fulfillment centers, blending experiential retail with Shopify POS, lifting repeat purchase rates to 42%. Customer-centric plays: Loyalty program expansion (NovaPrime, 18 million members) smoothed off-peaks, with LTV up 14% to $450, offsetting 10% CAC rise. Regional tailoring: U.S. focus on Gen Z via TikTok Shop (15% of traffic); APAC localization with 11.11 promotions; EMEA sustainability pushes amid EU Green Deal regs.

Looking to FY2024, we guide Q4 GMV at $1.95–2.05 billion (15–20% YoY growth), with full-year at $4.6–4.8 billion. Deviations will be minimal, as our 20% capex in predictive analytics positions us ahead of inflationary pressures and potential Fed pauses. We're not just riding waves—we're engineering them.

As we dive into the drivers behind our Q2 results, I'd like to spend a few minutes on the effectiveness of our marketing campaigns, with a particular focus on brand awareness and customer acquisition. In an industry where customer attention is fragmented across Amazon, Shopify-powered independents, TikTok Shop, and emerging social commerce platforms, our disciplined, data-driven approach has delivered outsized results. We've not only scaled awareness but also optimized acquisition economics in a high-inflation, cookie-deprecating environment.

Let me start with brand awareness. According to our latest Kantar survey of 5,000 online shoppers across key demographics, aided brand recall climbed 28% year-over-year to 47%—putting us on par with mid-tier players like ASOS or Zappos, and closing the gap on category leaders like Shein in fast fashion. Unaided recall among Gen Z (18-24) surged 42% to 22%, driven by our Forge Your Style multimedia campaign launched in June. This integrated push across Meta's Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and Pinterest—leveraging shoppable posts—generated 1.2 billion impressions globally, with a 15% lift in search volume for ShopNova on Google Trends.

Regionally, this played out differently. In North America, which accounts for 62% of our revenue, awareness hit 55% aided recall, up from 41% last year, fueled by targeted TV spots during NFL primetime and partnerships with influencers like Emma Chamberlain (3.5M followers). In Europe, post-Brexit logistics headwinds notwithstanding, we saw a 35% YoY increase to 38% recall, thanks to localized campaigns on Zalando and our GDPR-compliant first-party data stack. APAC was the star, with awareness jumping 52% to 29% in markets like Indonesia and India, where we integrated with Shopee and Flipkart via affiliate programs—capturing share from Temu's aggressive discounting.

Technically, this wasn't luck; it's the fruit of our AI-powered marketing engine, built on Google Cloud's Vertex AI and our proprietary ShopNova DMP (Data Management Platform). We've shifted 70% of spend to machine learning-optimized bidding on Google Performance Max and Meta Advantage+, achieving a 22% improvement in viewability scores. Post-third-party cookie phaseout, our 85% consent rate on first-party data—via server-side tagging and contextual targeting—has insulated us from signal loss, unlike some peers reporting 20-30% drops in attribution accuracy.

Now, turning to customer acquisition, where the real ROI shines. We added 2.8 million new customers in Q2, a 22% increase quarter-over-quarter and 19% YoY, bringing our active user base to 45 million. This translated to a 14% bump in new customer revenue to $320 million, with average order value (AOV) for newbies holding steady at $85—buoyed by personalized upsell prompts using our recommendation engine, which mirrors Amazon's but with 18% higher click-through rates (CTR) via collaborative filtering.

Critically, our customer acquisition cost (CAC) fell 17% YoY to $42, down from $51, yielding an industry-leading LTV:CAC ratio of 4.1x (LTV calculated at $172 over 24 months, factoring in 28% repeat purchase rate). Return on ad spend (ROAS) averaged 4.8x across channels—5.2x on paid search (Google Ads CPA at $28), 4.5x on social (TikTok For Business drove 40% of APAC newbies at 6x ROAS), and 3.9x on email/SMS via Klaviyo automation. For context, eMarketer benchmarks put median e-commerce ROAS at 3.2x; we're materially ahead.

Key campaigns underpinning this: Our Flash Forge event generated $150 million in incremental sales from 1.1 million new customers—a 25% YoY uplift—via dynamic pricing and live-streaming on our app, akin to what NTWRK does in streetwear. Influencer partnerships with 500 micro-influencers (10k-100k followers) delivered $12 ROAS per $1 spent, outperforming macro deals by 3x due to authenticity signals in our attribution model. And in a nod to sustainability trends—critical as 62% of millennials prioritize eco-brands per Nielsen—we rolled out Green Cart messaging, tying recycled packaging to a 12% conversion lift among eco-conscious segments.

Strategically, we're doubling down on omnichannel convergence. With social commerce projected to hit 17% of US e-retail by 2025 (per eMarketer), we've allocated 35% of our $250 million Q4 marketing budget to shoppable TikTok and Instagram—up from 20% last year. We're also piloting zero-party data plays like preference quizzes, aiming to drop CAC another 10% in H1 2025. Competitively, while Amazon's Prime Day loomed large, our agile targeting of their long-tail categories (e.g., mid-range electronics and sustainable apparel) netted 15% share gain in those SKUs.

Looking forward, expect continued momentum: Q4 guidance embeds 20-25% new customer growth, with ROAS targeting 5x+. We're investing $50 million in a cookieless CTV (Connected TV) platform with The Trade Desk, and expanding APAC via JioMart integrations in India.

In summary, our marketing is firing on all cylinders—building a moat through awareness while acquiring profitably. This positions ShopNova for sustained 25%+ top-line growth in a maturing e-commerce landscape.

Today, I'd like to dive deep into one of our key performance levers: advertising and marketing spend efficiency, specifically Return on Ad Spend, or ROAS. For those unfamiliar, ROAS is a critical metric in our industry, calculated as ad-attributed revenue divided by ad spend—essentially, how many dollars of revenue we generate for every dollar invested in advertising. A ROAS above 4x is industry benchmark for sustainable profitability in e-commerce, covering our typical 20-25% gross margins after fulfillment and returns.

In Q2, we delivered a blended ROAS of 4.7x, up 12% year-over-year from 4.2x in Q2 2023 and sequentially improved from 4.5x in Q1 2024. This represents approximately $4.7 billion in ad-attributed revenue on $1 billion in total ad spend, contributing over 35% to our overall quarterly GMV of $4.2 billion. Excluding our emerging high-growth categories like quick-commerce groceries—which naturally carry a lower ROAS of around 3.2x due to higher AOV sensitivity and competitive bidding—our core fashion and electronics segments achieved a robust 5.1x ROAS. This efficiency underpinned our 18% YoY revenue growth while keeping blended marketing expenses at 11.2% of GMV, down from 12.8% last year.

Let me break this down by channel, as we've continued to optimize our mix toward high-incrementality performance marketing amid a challenging macro environment. Google Ads, including Performance Max campaigns, remains our largest channel at 42% of spend, delivering a stellar 5.4x ROAS—up from 4.9x YoY—thanks to enhanced value-based bidding powered by our proprietary first-party data signals. We've layered in Google's latest PMax updates with audience signals from our loyalty program, which boasts 85 million members, driving a 22% lift in conversion rates for high-LTV segments like repeat apparel buyers.

Social commerce channels were a bright spot, with Meta platforms (Facebook and Instagram Shops) at 4.1x ROAS on 28% of spend, recovering from iOS 14.5+ attribution losses through Advantage+ Shopping Campaigns and our heavy investment in server-side tagging. TikTok Shop, now 15% of our mix, exploded to 6.8x ROAS—our highest performer—fueled by shoppertainment trends in Gen Z categories like beauty and streetwear. We ran over 5,000 creator-led live streams in Q2, mimicking Shein's playbook, with incrementality tests showing 35% uplift in purchase intent. Amazon DSP and Walmart Connect rounded out the rest, averaging 4.6x ROAS, where we're leveraging offsite retargeting to capture demand from their 500+ million combined users.

Regionally, performance varied based on market maturity and regulatory headwinds. In North America, which accounts for 55% of our ad spend, we hit 5.2x ROAS, bolstered by strong Black Friday-influenced carryover demand and our U.S.-exclusive partnerships with influencers like MrBeast for electronics drops. Europe lagged at 4.0x ROAS—impacted by GDPR cookie deprecation and rising CPMs from inflation-hit consumers—but we're countering this with 25% more investment in our owned retail media network, ShopNova Ads, which yielded 7.2x ROAS internally by monetizing publisher inventory from partners like Vogue and ASOS affiliates. APAC shone at 5.0x ROAS, driven by TikTok dominance in Southeast Asia (think Indonesia and Vietnam, where we compete head-on with Shopee and Lazada) and Baidu/Kuaishou in China, where live-streaming sales hit 28% of regional GMV.

What drove these gains? Technologically, we've accelerated our stack with AI-native optimizations. Our in-house MartAI Optimizer—built on TensorFlow and integrated with Snowflake for real-time data lakes—automates 70% of bidding decisions across channels, incorporating multi-touch attribution models like data-driven incrementality to filter out cannibalized sales. Post-Google's third-party cookie phaseout, we've doubled down on contextual targeting and contextual signals from our 2 billion+ monthly site visits, achieving a 15% ROAS uplift in privacy-safe environments. On the creative side, dynamic product ads with UGC from our 10 million UGC creators have boosted CTRs by 28%, particularly for impulse categories like fast fashion during peak seasons.

Strategically, we're shifting from broad awareness to hyper-performance marketing, targeting a sustainable 5x+ blended ROAS by year-end. This includes expanding our retail media business—now at $250 million annualized run-rate, akin to Criteo's model but verticalized for e-com—to offset rising platform fees from Meta and Google, which climbed 14% YoY. We're piloting shoppable CTV via Roku and Amazon Fire TV for living-room commerce, with early tests showing 4.5x ROAS at lower CPMs. CAC remains disciplined at $28 per new customer, with LTV/CAC ratios holding at 3.8x, ensuring long-term unit economics even as consumer wallets tighten amid 4-5% global inflation.

Looking ahead, Q3 guidance assumes 4.8x-5.0x ROAS, factoring in back-to-school ramps and holiday pre-loading, though we remain vigilant on ad fatigue and auction dynamics. We'll continue allocating 60% of incremental spend to top-ROAS channels like TikTok and our owned media, while testing emerging formats like WhatsApp Flows in Brazil for conversational commerce.

In summary, our ROAS trajectory underscores ShopNova's operational excellence in a maturing e-commerce landscape, where winners like us prioritize data moats and incrementality over vanity metrics. Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. Limit your questions to one per caller. Our first question comes from Sarah Kline with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Kline:
Thanks for taking my question. Taylor, your commentary on seasonality was detailed—can you expand on the Q2 positive deviation and how you're mitigating potential Q3 risks from supply chain issues like Red Sea disruptions?

Jamie Chen:
Thanks, Sarah. Great question. The Q2 acceleration to 18% YoY GMV was indeed a positive surprise, largely due to NovaPredict AI's personalization boost amid Prime Day tailwinds, which lifted AOV and countered softer macro trends. For Q3, we're well-positioned against supply chain headwinds; our air freight shifts and vendor-direct models have kept on-time delivery at 98.5%, even as freight costs rose. We've also localized inventory in APAC for events like Singles Day, minimizing deviations. Morgan can add on ops if needed, but we're confident in our 10-12% QoQ guide.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel:
Hi, team. On the marketing side, Taylor, your ROAS improvements are impressive at 4.7x blended. Can you talk more about channel shifts, especially TikTok's role, and sustainability in a higher CPM environment?

Taylor Brooks:
Absolutely, Raj. TikTok Shop at 6.8x ROAS was a standout, driven by 5,000 live streams targeting Gen Z in beauty and streetwear, with 35% incrementality uplift. We've shifted 15% of spend there from Meta, where Advantage+ helped recover to 4.1x. Amid 14% YoY CPM inflation, our AI optimizer automates bidding with first-party data, delivering 15% ROAS gains in cookieless setups. Owned media like ShopNova Ads at 7.2x further insulates us. Expect 5x+ by year-end as we scale CTV pilots.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. Jamie or Morgan, on customer acquisition effectiveness, you added 2.8 million new customers with CAC down to $42. How is this flowing through to repeat rates, and any updates on NovaPrime loyalty?

Morgan Lee:
Hi Lisa, thanks. Our 4.1x LTV:CAC reflects strong acquisition, with new customer AOV steady at $85 via AI upsells. Repeats are at 62% in NA, up thanks to NovaPrime's 18 million members—LTV now $450, up 14%. We've enhanced it with Braze campaigns and Green Cart messaging, lifting NPS 8 points and conversions 12% in eco-segments. This smooths seasonality, with 42% repeat rates overall. Early NovaPredict traction is pushing 28% repeat YoY.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jamie Chen for closing remarks.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Seasonality impact: Analyze trends and explain deviations.
GMV growth (YoY and QoQ): Report actuals vs. guidance.
Effectiveness of marketing campaigns: Brand awareness and customer acquisition.
Advertising and marketing spend efficiency: Return on ad spend (ROAS).

aspect_summary.Seasonality impact: Pronounced seasonality with Q4 peaking at 42% of annual GMV, off-peak Q1-Q2 at 18-22%; trends show consistent YoY growth in peaks (e.g., Q4 28%) and stability off-peak; deviations include Q1 FY2024 -3% YoY due to inflation (mitigated by inventory optimization), Q2 +18% YoY acceleration from NovaPredict AI and Prime Day, Q3 flat YoY offset by air freight and vendor-direct fulfillment; de-risked via AI pricing, omnichannel, loyalty programs.
aspect_summary.GMV growth (YoY and QoQ): Q2 GMV $4.2B, +22% YoY (beat 14-17% guidance), +12% QoQ from Q1 $3.75B (beat 5-7% guidance); driven by category surges (fashion +28%, beauty +45%), regional strength (NA +25%, APAC +35%), AI personalization, technical upgrades; raised FY GMV to $18-19B, Q3 ~$4.5-4.6B (10-12% QoQ).
aspect_summary.Effectiveness of marketing campaigns: Brand awareness up with aided recall +28% YoY to 47% (Gen Z unaided +42% to 22%), driven by Forge Your Style campaign (1.2B impressions); customer acquisition added 2.8M new customers (+22% QoQ, +19% YoY), new revenue +14% to $320M, CAC -17% YoY to $42, LTV:CAC 4.1x; key campaigns like Flash Forge ($150M incremental), influencers (12x ROAS).
aspect_summary.Advertising and marketing spend efficien: Blended ROAS 4.7x (+12% YoY from 4.2x, + from Q1 4.5x), generating $4.7B revenue on $1B spend (35% of GMV); channels: Google 5.4x, Meta 4.1x, TikTok 6.8x; regional: NA 5.2x, Europe 4.0x, APAC 5.0x; improvements via AI bidding (MartAI), first-party data, dynamic ads; targeting 5x+ by year-end.
